paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: Suppose you are invited to put forward a proposal to the university on how to make students’ campus life easier. You are now to write an essay to make your proposal. You will have 30 minutes to write the essay. You should write at least 120 words but not more than 180 words.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：假设您被邀请向大学提出一份关于如何让学生的校园生活更轻松的提案。你现在要写一篇文章来提出你的建议。你将有 30 分钟的时间来写这篇文章。您应该写至少 120 个字但不超过 180 个字。

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: In this section, you will hear three news reports. At the end of each news report, you will hear two or three questions. Both the news report and the questions will be spoken only once. After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C and D. Then mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 1 with a single line through the centre.

You are required to select one word for each blank from a list of choices given in a word bank following the passage. Read the passage through carefully before making your choices. Each choice in the bank is identified by a letter. Please mark the corresponding letter for each item on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre. You may not use any of the words in the bank more than once.

paragraphs.sourceText: It may sound surprising, but people who are supersensitive to coffee’s bitter taste actually drink more of it, a new study finds.
paragraphs.translationZh: 这听起来可能令人惊讶，但一项新的研究发现，对咖啡苦味超级敏感的人实际上会喝更多的咖啡。

paragraphs.sourceText: This sensitivity isn’t 26 a matter of taste, either, but rather is influenced by a person’s genetic makeup, the researchers said in the study.
paragraphs.translationZh: 研究人员在研究中表示，这种敏感性也不仅仅是品味问题，而是受到一个人基因构成的影响。

paragraphs.sourceText: “You’d expect that people who are particularly sensitive to the bitter taste of caffeine would drink less coffee,” said study senior researcher Marilyn Cornelis. “The 27 results of our study suggest coffee consumers acquire a taste for or an ability to detect the bitterness of caffeine due to the learned positive 28 brought out by caffeine.”
paragraphs.translationZh: 研究高级研究员玛丽莲·科内利斯 (Marilyn Cornelis) 表示：“你可能会认为，对咖啡因苦味特别敏感的人会少喝咖啡。” “我们研究的相反结果表明，由于咖啡因带来的习得性积极强化，咖啡消费者获得了对咖啡因苦味的味道或能力。”

paragraphs.sourceText: Put another way, people who have a 29 ability to taste the bitterness of coffee learn to associate “good things with it,” Cornelis said. This finding is surprising, given that bitterness often serves as a warning mechanism to 30 people to spit out harmful substances, the scientists said.
paragraphs.translationZh: 换句话说，那些品尝咖啡苦味的能力更强的人会学会将“好的东西与咖啡联系起来”，科内利斯说。科学家们表示，这一发现令人惊讶，因为苦味常常作为一种警告机制，说服人们吐出有害物质。

paragraphs.sourceText: Researchers conducted the study to understand how genetics influences people’s 31 of tea, coffee and alcohol which tend to taste bitter, said lead study researcher Jue Sheng Ong.
paragraphs.translationZh: 首席研究员 Jue Shen Ong 表示，研究人员进行这项研究的目的是了解基因如何影响人们对茶、咖啡和酒精的摄入，而这些茶、咖啡和酒精的味道往往是苦的。

paragraphs.sourceText: “While all bitter flavors may seem the same, we 32 the bitterness of Brussels sprouts (抱子甘蓝), quinine (奎宁) and caffeine 33 ,” Ong told Live Science. “The degree to which we find these flavors bitter is, in part, determined by your genes.”
paragraphs.translationZh: “虽然所有的苦味看起来都一样，但我们分别感知到抱子甘蓝、奎宁和咖啡因的苦味，”Ong 告诉 Live Science。 “我们发现这些味道的苦味程度部分取决于你的基因。”

paragraphs.sourceText: People with the genes to taste the bitterness of green vegetables are more likely to prefer tea to coffee. In 34 , people who were more sensitive to quinine’s bitter flavors and those found in green vegetables tended to 35 coffee.
paragraphs.translationZh: 具有品尝绿色蔬菜苦味基因的人更有可能更喜欢茶而不是咖啡。此外，对奎宁的苦味和绿色蔬菜中的苦味更敏感的人往往会避免喝咖啡。

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: In this section, you are going to read a passage with ten statements attached to it. Each statement contains information given in one of the paragraphs. Identify the paragraph from which the information is derived. You may choose a paragraph more than once. Each paragraph is marked with a letter. Answer the questions by marking the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：在本节中，您将阅读一段附有十个陈述的段落。每条陈述都包含其中一个段落中给出的信息。确定信息来源的段落。您可以多次选择一个段落。每个段落都标有一个字母。通过在答题卡 2 上标记相应的字母来回答问题。

paragraphs.sourceText: Exercise and Dementia
paragraphs.translationZh: 运动与痴呆症

paragraphs.sourceText: A) If this doesn’t encourage you to squeeze in a workout today, nothing will: a new study from Sweden shows that women who were highly fit in mid-life were nearly 90% less likely to get dementia (失智) decades later.
paragraphs.translationZh: 答）如果这不能鼓励您今天挤出时间锻炼，那就没有什么可以了：瑞典的一项新研究表明，中年时身体健康的女性几十年后患痴呆症的可能性降低近 90%。

paragraphs.sourceText: B) After initial exercise tests in middle age, researchers followed the women for 44 years. Both groups lived just as long, but those who could ride an exercise bike at a fast rate for 6 minutes in the initial test had a much lower risk of dementia later on than those who couldn’t complete the workout.
paragraphs.translationZh: B) 在中年时期进行初步运动测试后，研究人员对这些女性进行了 44 年的跟踪调查。两组人的寿命都一样长，但那些在最初测试中能够快速骑自行车 6 分钟的人，后来患痴呆症的风险比那些无法完成锻炼的人要低得多。

paragraphs.sourceText: C) The study, published Wednesday in the journal Neurology, couldn’t prove that exercise prevented dementia, and the findings aren’t a surprise — it’s long been known there’s a correlation between exercise and decreased dementia risk — but the results were particularly dramatic. About 5% of the women with the highest peak workload — those who were able to bike the hardest over those 6 minutes — developed dementia, compared to 25% of those with medium fitness and 45% who weren’t fit enough to finish the test, the study found. Overall, women who were highly fit compared to those who were moderately fit decreased their risk of dementia by 88%. The few highly fit women who did develop dementia became symptomatic at age 90 on average, 11 years later than the moderately fit.
paragraphs.translationZh: C) 周三发表在《神经病学》杂志上的这项研究无法证明运动可以预防痴呆症，研究结果并不令人意外——人们早就知道运动和降低痴呆症风险之间存在相关性——但结果尤其引人注目。研究发现，在峰值工作量最高的女性（那些能够在这 6 分钟内最努力地骑自行车的女性）中，约有 5% 患上了痴呆症，而中等健康水平的女性和体质不足以完成测试的女性中，这一比例分别为 25% 和 45%。总体而言，与中等健康的女性相比，高度健康的女性患痴呆症的风险降低了 88%。少数高度健康的女性确实患上了痴呆症，平均在 90 岁时出现症状，比中等健康的女性晚了 11 年。

paragraphs.sourceText: D) “I’m very surprised that the finding was so strong,” said Ingmar Skoog, the paper’s senior author and a psychiatry (精神病学) professor at the University of Gothenburg in Sweden. “It really shows the importance of exercise.”
paragraphs.translationZh: D) 该论文的资深作者、瑞典哥德堡大学精神病学教授 Ingmar Skoog 说：“这一发现如此有力，我感到非常惊讶。” “这确实表明了锻炼的重要性。”

paragraphs.sourceText: E) Dementia, as defined in medical dictionaries, is a broad term that describes a loss of thinking ability, memory, attention, logical reasoning, and other mental abilities. These changes are severe enough to interfere with social or occupational functioning. Dementia isn’t a disease. Instead, it’s a group of symptoms caused by other conditions. It happens when the parts of your brain used for learning, memory, decision making, and language are damaged or diseased. About 5% – 8% of adults over age 65 have some form of dementia. This percentage doubles every 5 years after 65. As many as half of people in their 80s have some dementia.
paragraphs.translationZh: E) 根据医学词典的定义，痴呆症是一个广义术语，描述思维能力、记忆力、注意力、逻辑推理和其他心理能力的丧失。这些变化严重到足以干扰社会或职业功能。痴呆症不是一种疾病。相反，它是由其他条件引起的一组症状。当大脑中用于学习、记忆、决策和语言的部分受损或患病时，就会发生这种情况。大约 5% – 8% 的 65 岁以上成年人患有某种形式的痴呆症。 65 岁以后，这一比例每 5 年翻一番。 80 多岁的人中有多达一半患有某种程度的痴呆症。

paragraphs.sourceText: F) Dementia is not temporary confusion or forgetfulness that might result from an infection that heals without treatment. It can also come from an underlying (潜在的) illness or side effects of medications. Dementia typically gets worse over time. People with dementia have problems with thinking and remembering that affect their ability to manage their daily life.
paragraphs.translationZh: F) 痴呆症不是因感染而无需治疗即可治愈的暂时性混乱或健忘。它也可能来自潜在的疾病或药物的副作用。痴呆症通常会随着时间的推移而恶化。痴呆症患者的思维和记忆存在问题，影响他们管理日常生活的能力。

paragraphs.sourceText: G) Dementia is typically associated with declines in cognitive function. Yet researchers have found an association between dementia and declines in hearing and other basic sensory functions.
paragraphs.translationZh: G) 痴呆症通常与认知功能下降有关。然而研究人员发现痴呆症与听力和其他基本感觉功能下降之间存在关联。

paragraphs.sourceText: H) Though the study mentioned above was fairly small (only 191 women took the initial fitness test, which means it’s hard to maintain statistical significance while breaking the group down into subcategories of more or less fit), it does give us hope that dementia can be prevented or delayed through exercise in one’s middle age.
paragraphs.translationZh: H) 虽然上述研究规模相当小（只有 191 名女性参加了最初的体能测试，这意味着在将群体分为或多或少适合的子类别时很难保持统计显着性），但它确实给了我们希望，通过中年锻炼可以预防或延缓痴呆症。

paragraphs.sourceText: I) Alzheimer’s (阿尔茨海默病) and other dementias are believed to begin 15 – 20 years before symptoms even appear, so it makes sense that exercising in mid-life would affect the risk, Skoog said. Exercise alone is not likely to prevent Alzheimer’s, but the study shows people are not helpless in the face of one of the most feared, costliest and common diseases of old age, he added. And the same activities that help prevent Alzheimer’s — including avoiding smoking, getting adequate exercise and sleep and eating a healthy diet — also prevent heart disease, he said, making them even more worthwhile. “You can do something yourself to decrease your odds,” Skoog said.
paragraphs.translationZh: I) 阿尔茨海默病和其他痴呆症被认为在症状出现前 15 至 20 年就开始出现，因此中年锻炼会影响患病风险是有道理的，Skoog 说。他补充说，仅靠锻炼不太可能预防阿尔茨海默病，但研究表明，面对老年最可怕、最昂贵和最常见的疾病之一，人们并非束手无策。他说，有助于预防阿尔茨海默氏症的活动——包括避免吸烟、充足的锻炼和睡眠以及健康的饮食——也可以预防心脏病，这使得这些活动更有价值。 “你可以自己做一些事情来降低几率，”斯科格说。

paragraphs.sourceText: J) Maintaining a healthy lifestyle in mid-life, decades before disease sets in, makes sense, said David Knopman, a fellow of the American Academy of Neurology, who was not involved in the study. “I suspect it’s a dose,” said Knopman, also associate director of the Alzheimer’s Disease Research Center at Mayo Clinic in Rochester, Minnesota. “Starting in late life is better than not starting at all, but starting in mid-life seems to offer a larger benefit.”
paragraphs.translationZh: J) 美国神经病学学会研究员大卫·诺普曼（David Knopman）表示，在中年时期（疾病发病前几十年）保持健康的生活方式是有意义的，他没有参与这项研究。 “我怀疑这是一个剂量，”明尼苏达州罗彻斯特梅奥诊所阿尔茨海默病研究中心副主任诺普曼说。 “晚年开始总比不开始好，但中年开始似乎能带来更大的好处。”

paragraphs.sourceText: K) Although it is not entirely clear why exercise helps put off or prevent Alzheimer’s, Knopman said it’s likely that exercise maintains good blood flow to the brain. “When the brain is healthier from a vascular (血管的) point of view, it can absorb more Alzheimer’s pathogen (病原体) before people become symptomatic,” he said.
paragraphs.translationZh: K）虽然尚不完全清楚为什么运动有助于推迟或预防阿尔茨海默氏症，但诺普曼表示，运动很可能可以维持流向大脑的良好血液流动。 “从血管的角度来看，当大脑更健康时，它可以在人们出现症状之前吸收更多的阿尔茨海默病病原体，”他说。

paragraphs.sourceText: L) The message isn’t that everyone needs to run marathons in middle age, Knopman said, but a healthy lifestyle pays off.
paragraphs.translationZh: L）诺普曼说，这并不是说每个人都需要在中年跑马拉松，而是健康的生活方式是有回报的。

paragraphs.sourceText: M) This type of study can’t say exactly what kind of exercise is best, or how much is needed — only a study that has a placebo (安慰剂) group and tracks people going forward can do that, said Keith Fargo, director of scientific programs and outreach at the non-profit Alzheimer’s Association. “The literature has not yet settled on an amount or type of exercise that is going to be key, although the bulk of literature has suggested that aerobic (有氧的) exercise is what you need to be doing,” he said. That doesn’t mean you have to compete in marathons but “more than a 10-min dog walk” would be a good idea, Fargo said.
paragraphs.translationZh: M）非营利性阿尔茨海默氏症协会科学项目和外展部主任基思·法戈（Keith Fargo）表示，此类研究无法准确说明哪种运动最好，或者需要多少运动量，只有安慰剂组并跟踪人们的进展情况的研究才能做到这一点。 “文献尚未确定关键的运动量或运动类型，尽管大量文献表明有氧运动是你需要做的，”他说。法戈说，这并不意味着你必须参加马拉松比赛，但“遛狗 10 分钟以上”将是一个好主意。

paragraphs.sourceText: N) Several lifestyle studies are getting underway soon, including one backed by the Alzheimer’s Association called the U.S. POINTER study, which will offer at-risk adults, ages 60 – 79, a series of lifestyle interventions (干预) to see if they impact Alzheimer’s risk. That and other Alzheimer’s-related studies are always looking for volunteers to participate, he said.
paragraphs.translationZh: N) 几项生活方式研究即将展开，其中包括由阿尔茨海默病协会支持的一项名为“U.S. POINTER”研究，该研究将为 60 至 79 岁的高危成年人提供一系列生活方式干预措施，看看它们是否会影响阿尔茨海默病的风险。他说，这项研究和其他与阿尔茨海默病相关的研究一直在寻找志愿者参与。

paragraphs.sourceText: O) In the next three to five years, these studies should allow researchers to provide clearer recommendations for exercise and other lifestyle modifications that might reduce Alzheimer’s risk, such as sleep, diet and social activities, Fargo said. But it’s already quite clear that exercising at any point in life is better for your brain than not exercising at all, Fargo added.
paragraphs.translationZh: O）法戈说，在未来三到五年内，这些研究应该能让研究人员为锻炼和其他可能降低阿尔茨海默病风险的生活方式改变提供更明确的建议，例如睡眠、饮食和社交活动。但法戈补充说，很明显，在生命中的任何阶段锻炼都比完全不锻炼对大脑更好。

paragraphs.sourceText: P. “If you don’t want to have dementia when you’re 80, the time to start getting fit is now,” he said. “It may not necessarily give you a longer life, but there’s a compelling body of work that it will give you more good years.”
paragraphs.translationZh: P. “如果你不想在 80 岁时患上痴呆症，那么现在就是开始健身的时候了，”他说。 “它不一定能让你活得更长，但有大量令人信服的工作可以让你拥有更多美好的岁月。”

paragraphs.sourceText: 36. It is typical for dementia to worsen with the passage of time.
paragraphs.translationZh: 36. 痴呆症通常会随着时间的推移而恶化。

paragraphs.sourceText: 37. According to Knopman, the study gives the message that a healthy lifestyle is beneficial, but not that all the middle-aged need heavy exercise.
paragraphs.translationZh: 37. 根据诺普曼的说法，这项研究传达的信息是，健康的生活方式是有益的，但并不是所有中年人都需要大量锻炼。

paragraphs.sourceText: 38. The results of a new study will encourage middle-aged women to find time exercising however busy they are.
paragraphs.translationZh: 38. 一项新研究的结果将鼓励中年女性无论多么忙碌都要抽出时间锻炼身体。

paragraphs.sourceText: 39. Hopefully, one can postpone or prevent dementia by exercising in their mid-life.
paragraphs.translationZh: 39. 希望人们能够通过中年锻炼来推迟或预防痴呆症。

paragraphs.sourceText: 40. In a few years, researchers should be able to offer clearer advice on exercise and other lifestyle changes for reducing the incidence of Alzheimer’s.
paragraphs.translationZh: 40. 几年后，研究人员应该能够就锻炼和其他生活方式的改变提供更明确的建议，以降低阿尔茨海默病的发病率。

paragraphs.sourceText: 41. Dementia refers to a loss of multiple mental abilities such as memory and logical reasoning.
paragraphs.translationZh: 41. 痴呆症是指记忆力和逻辑推理等多种心理能力的丧失。

paragraphs.sourceText: 42. One researcher believes that exercise may keep the brain well supplied with blood.
paragraphs.translationZh: 42. 一位研究人员认为，运动可以使大脑保持良好的血液供应。

paragraphs.sourceText: 43. Medical literature has not concluded as to what exercise or how much exercise is crucial, although it generally agrees that people should do aerobic exercise.
paragraphs.translationZh: 43. 医学文献尚未得出什么运动或运动量至关重要的结论，尽管它普遍认为人们应该进行有氧运动。

paragraphs.sourceText: 44. It has long been common knowledge that exercise correlates with reduced risk of dementia.
paragraphs.translationZh: 44. 长期以来，人们都知道锻炼与降低痴呆风险相关。

paragraphs.sourceText: 45. Activities helpful in the prevention of Alzheimer’s also prevent heart disease.

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 46 to 50 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 46 至 50 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: People who systematically underestimate themselves and their own performance suffer from the so-called Impostor Phenomenon. They think that any success is due to external circumstances or just luck and chance. Those people live in constant fear that their “deception” will be exposed.
paragraphs.translationZh: 系统性地低估自己和自己的表现的人会遭受所谓的“冒名顶替现象”。他们认为任何成功都是由于外部环境或者只是运气和机会。这些人一直生活在恐惧之中，担心他们的“欺骗”会被揭露。

paragraphs.sourceText: It is common for people to question their abilities now and again. A healthy amount of reflection and self-doubt can protect a person from acting impulsively. However, there are people who are permanently plagued by a massive amount of self-doubt despite delivering a good performance. They think that all of their successes are not a product of their skill or hard work, instead they attribute their own successes to external circumstances, for example, to luck and chance, or believe that their performance is massively overestimated by others. Failures, on the other hand, are always internalised as the result of their own shortcomings.
paragraphs.translationZh: 人们时不时质疑自己的能力是很常见的。适量的反思和自我怀疑可以防止一个人做出冲动的行为。然而，有些人尽管表现出色，却永远受到大量自我怀疑的困扰。他们认为自己所有的成功都不是自己技能或努力工作的结果，而是将自己的成功归因于外部环境，例如运气和机会，或者认为自己的表现被他人大大高估了。另一方面，失败总是被内化为自身缺点的结果。

paragraphs.sourceText: Psychologists from Martin Luther University Halle-Wittenberg examined the topic for the first time under real-life conditions. Seventy-six participants completed a range of intelligence tests and received positive feedback on them, regardless of their actual performance. They were then asked why they think they did so well.
paragraphs.translationZh: 哈勒维滕贝格马丁路德大学的心理学家首次在现实生活条件下研究了这个话题。七十六名参与者完成了一系列智力测试，并收到了积极的反馈，无论他们的实际表现如何。然后他们被问到为什么他们认为自己做得这么好。

paragraphs.sourceText: The study showed two things: First, the self-reported degree of Impostor Phenomenon is not related to actual measured intelligence or performance. Secondly, the test supported the assumption that people with a tendency to exhibit the Impostor Phenomenon devalue their objectively measured performance and attribute positive results to external causes such as luck and chance, but not to their own abilities. These results are also completely unrelated to age and gender.
paragraphs.translationZh: 该研究表明了两件事：首先，自我报告的冒名顶替现象程度与实际测量的智力或表现无关。其次，该测试支持这样的假设：有冒名顶替现象倾向的人会贬低他们客观衡量的表现，并将积极的结果归因于运气和机会等外部原因，而不是归因于他们自己的能力。这些结果也与年龄和性别完全无关。

paragraphs.sourceText: A permanent underestimation of one’s own abilities is often accompanied by the fear that this supposed intellectual deception will be exposed sooner or later and that they will pay the price for this. The Impostor Phenomenon was first described in 1978 by U.S. psychologists Pauline Clance and Suzanne Imes. They observed that there is a particularly high number of successful women who do not think they are very intelligent. The Impostor Phenomenon is not defined as a mental illness. However, people who suffer from it show a higher vulnerability to depression.
paragraphs.translationZh: 对自己能力的永久低估常常伴随着这样的恐惧：这种所谓的智力欺骗迟早会被揭露，他们会为此付出代价。冒充者现象最早由美国心理学家 Pauline Clance 和 Suzanne Imes 于 1978 年描述。他们观察到，有相当多的成功女性并不认为自己很聪明。冒充者现象并不被定义为精神疾病。然而，患有抑郁症的人更容易患抑郁症。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 51 to 55 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 问题 51 至 55 基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: Music is a universal language. In every culture and country, you will find music. It is vitally important across the globe and has the potential to bring people together in peace and harmony. One of my favorite experiences in music is seeing musicians from different cultures come together and perform as a group. When each culture brings its own unique qualities to the group, an entirely new sound is achieved. This can create extraordinary results. People can communicate with each other using music as the common language.
paragraphs.translationZh: 音乐是一种通用语言。在每一种文化和每一个国家，你都会发现音乐。它在全球范围内至关重要，并且有潜力使人们和平与和谐地聚集在一起。我最喜欢的音乐经历之一就是看到来自不同文化的音乐家聚集在一起并作为一个团体表演。当每种文化为群体带来自己独特的品质时，就会产生全新的声音。这可以创造非凡的成果。人们可以用音乐作为共同语言来相互交流。

paragraphs.sourceText: One common musical thread between cultures is known as the pentatonic scale. It is astonishing how many cultures share this tool in approaching music. The pentatonic scale consists of five notes; “penta-” meaning 5, and “tonic” meaning tone or note. This scale can be found in music everywhere including that of Native Americans, Africans, and Asians. It is also found in popular music, blues, jazz, and rock. Using this five-note scale, musicians from around the globe have a medium through which they can relate, communicate, perform, and ultimately understand each other.
paragraphs.translationZh: 不同文化之间的一种常见音乐线索被称为五声音阶。令人惊讶的是，有如此多的文化在接触音乐时共享这一工具。五声音阶由五个音符组成； “penta-”表示 5，“tonic”表示音调或音符。这种音阶随处可见，包括美洲原住民、非洲人和亚洲人的音乐。它也出现在流行音乐、布鲁斯、爵士乐和摇滚乐中。使用这个五音符音阶，来自世界各地的音乐家可以通过这种媒介进行联系、交流、表演并最终相互理解。

paragraphs.sourceText: Music is tied to specific perceptual (感知的), mental, and emotional faculties, including language (all societies put words to their songs), motor control (people in all societies dance), sound analysis (all musical systems have a distinct pitch and quality, and aesthetics (美感) (their tunes and rhythms are balanced between repetitiveness and chaos.
paragraphs.translationZh: 音乐与特定的感知、心理和情感能力联系在一起，包括语言（所有社会都在歌曲中加入歌词）、运动控制（所有社会中的人们都在跳舞）、声音分析（所有音乐系统都有独特的音高和质量，以及美感）（它们的曲调和节奏在重复和混乱之间保持平衡。

paragraphs.sourceText: There is no known society that existed without music. Although each culture has their own specific style and approach to music, you will find that the purposes behind music are very similar across the board. Music essentially serves to express or change emotions. It can cheer you up, sadden you, anger you or excite you. Music is often ceremonial: used in religion, ceremony, and celebration. Music can simply be recreational: entertaining, joyful and fun. Any way you have used music, it is almost certain that every other culture has used music in the very same way. And that is something that bonds all of us. We all share a deep love for music and it has the power to unite us.
paragraphs.translationZh: 没有一个已知的社会是没有音乐而存在的。尽管每种文化都有自己特定的音乐风格和方法，但您会发现音乐背后的目的非常相似。音乐本质上是用来表达或改变情感的。它可以让你高兴，让你悲伤，让你愤怒，或者让你兴奋。音乐通常是仪式性的：用于宗教、仪式和庆祝活动。音乐可以只是娱乐性的：有趣、快乐和有趣。无论你以何种方式使用音乐，几乎可以肯定的是，所有其他文化都以同样的方式使用音乐。这是将我们所有人联系在一起的东西。我们都对音乐怀有深深的热爱，它有力量将我们团结在一起。
